newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound, waits for Japanese fund move.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound, waits for Japanese fund move.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound in late Asian trading as the market waited for funds movement from Japan in their new financial year beginning Tuesday, dealers said on Monday.
"If there is a movement of excess funds from Japan, it is likely that ringgit will get a substantial portion of it," said the head of dealing at a Malaysian bank.

Japanese funds and banks traditionally park their excess funds in high yielding currencies in their new financial year beginning April 1. In the last few years, Southeast Asian nations have been the main beneficiaries of this movement.
"If that does not happen, then we could see some fresh buying of the dollar," a dealer with another bank said.
He said there was some month-end dollar demand on Monday from Kuala Lumpur-based corporates, but volumes were low.
There was little impact of the Bank Negara annual report for 1996 released on Friday. It announced that monetary policy will remain tight and exchange rate would be left to market forces.
"The data is supportive of the ringgit. The market is also taking this as a hint that Malaysia would like to see a stronger ringgit," said an European bank dealer in Singapore.
Dealers said there was also some liquidation of long ringgit/Singapore dollar positions.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4794/04 a dollar and 1.7154/73 a Singapore dollar.
